episodes.title: The heading
episodes.english: Year 1 of the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes, the seventh of the name⟩, {living, enduring, strong}. Went to the West the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes, the sixth of the name⟩, [Lord of the River and of the Two Banks], beloved of Uqa'a, {fire of Uqa'a upon the mound, who stood, who was crowned, lord of the count, whose house is entered, whose seal is on the granary, whose grain the barges carry}, [given life like the sun forever], in his twenty-seventh year. His account is read.

episodes.title: Birth and crowning
episodes.english: Shaped him Uzn'era [in the womb], a child of the house of Zu'Meku. Stood he upon the mound [at Yath-Telgu]; {set the priesthood of Uqa'a the crown on him, and gave him his name, ⟨Meqes⟩; by this name every contract of the year is dated.} Qe'aret set truth in his mouth, and Reth'Sa'ar wrote his name [in the house of books]. The gods gave him life and dominion, like the sun.

episodes.title: The war of the west
episodes.english: Came down His Majesty, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, Lord of the River and of the Two Banks, given life like the sun forever,} upon the hill-men of the western margins, and Chaq'ur raged before him like the storm. Smote he their chieftains, [took he their herds,] and brought back their princes bound [beneath his sandals]. {The margins were the Gar-Au's.}

episodes.title: The war of the north and the tribute
episodes.english: Sailed he, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, given life like the sun forever,} against the raiders of the northern sea, and the fire of Uqa'a went out against their ships. The river was at peace, and the barges came up laden: gold, cedar, horses [and slaves]. {The river was the Gar-Au's.}

episodes.title: The great hunt and the lean years
episodes.english: Rode he out, {the Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a, Lord of the River and of the Two Banks,} against the river-horses that ravaged the herds and the fields, and the beasts taken were counted. In the years of the low river he opened the god's granaries under his seal, which he had filled in the years of the flood, and none of his people hungered.

episodes.title: His works, the god's answer, and the weighing
episodes.english: {The Gar-Au ⟨Meqes⟩, beloved of Uqa'a,} built anew the house of Uqa'a, gave it altars of gold, and endowed it with fields and herds. [He raised his Way at the head of the death-road at Zu-Gezer.] [Words spoken by Uqa'a, {fire on the first ground, lord of the dry ink, who comes up the road}: “My beloved son, I give you every land, every foreign country bowed beneath your sandals; I give you the years of the sun upon the throne of the mound.”] Before the gods the tablets lay level on the beam: what he owed was closed, and nothing remained; what was owed to him stood open. He went down owed.

ordinal.title: the sixth and the seventh of the name
ordinal.note: No sign writes an ordinal, and neither the design note nor the thalorna notes say how a regnal number is written in Zethu. Proposed: the strokes inside the oval after the name, six (16-027) for Meqes VI and seven (16-021) for Meqes VII, since the king-list numbers a throne name's bearers and the number belongs to the name. The alternative is the strokes just outside the oval's tie.

strong.title: living, enduring, strong
strong.note: From the stela's closing epithet. _Strong_ is 01-014, the standing man braced on a stave, whose consonants k-z are _kuz_, strong (the throne-name element in the Khelathi note).

bank.title: Two Banks
bank.note: No sign means a river bank. Written _the land, two_: 10-028 (land and a sprout) with the two strokes after it, as a count follows its noun in Zethu. 10-001 (current between two banks) already draws both banks, so an alternative is to drop the phrase into _Lord of the River_ alone.

fire.title: the fire of Uqa'a
fire.note: The fire is 09-015, smoke rising from a hearth (h). It is a hearth, not a weapon, and the sign carries no god of its own. Uqa'a's gloss is _fire_, so his sign alone could stand here instead.

stood.title: stood upon the mound
stood.note: The standing is written as the crowning it was: the crown of the Gar-Au (15-007) and the enthroned figure (01-060), then _upon the mound_. No sign shows a man standing on a mound.

countlord.title: lord of the count
countlord.note: The stela's _lord of the count_ is written _lord, of, the tally rod_ (01-013, 10-016, 13-035).

houseentered.title: whose house is entered
houseentered.note: Written _house, tablet_ (11-003, 14-018): the clay tablet stands for the entry, as in _his account is read_.

gravingseal.title: whose seal is on the granary, whose grain the barges carry
gravingseal.note: Written _seal, upon, granary; grain, barge_ (13-032, 10-016, 11-004; 14-016, 12-014). The relative _whose_ is unwritten.

give.title: given / I give you
give.note: No sign means _give_. 03-023, an open palm held above a bowed head, is the gesture of a superior conferring on a bowed recipient, and carries no god. It is the nearest honest sign; the plain hand (04-011) is the fallback.

like.title: like the sun
like.note: No sign means _like_, so the comparison is unwritten: _life, dominion, the sun_. 09-005 (the disk at the top of the arch) is used for the sun so that Uqa'a's own sign, 09-002, keeps its god's sense.

account.title: his account
account.note: 04-018, the heart bound with a cord and sealed (h-l-z), is _halzi_: the heart and the account it answers for. It writes _his account_ here and _owed_ at the end of register 6.

read.title: is read
read.note: No sign means _read aloud_. 03-005, a curl of breath leaving a mouth, writes speaking.

shaped.title: shaped him
shaped.note: No sign means _shape_. 01-026, the man at the wheel (g-th-r, _gethar_, potter), shows a potter forming a vessel. It is an image of making, not a word for it.

womb.title: in the womb
womb.note: No sign for the womb. Written _in the mother_ with 02-011, the seated lady in a long garment.

priesthood.title: the priesthood of Uqa'a
priesthood.note: Written as the sample inscription writes a priest, _Lem'Nelgir_: the kneeling servant (01-002, l-m, _lem_) and the seated god (03-001), with the plural strokes, then _of Uqa'a_.

plural.title: plural mark
plural.note: The three strokes (16-006) are the numeral three. Using them after a noun as the plural mark is the Egyptian convention, and no Zethu note states it. The fallback is to write a plural by repeating the sign.

contract.title: every contract
contract.note: No sign means a contract. 14-019, the sealed roll tied with a cord, is the nearest: a document closed under seal. The stela names contracts, tax rolls and leases; only the contract is written.

dated.title: is dated
dated.note: No sign means _to date_. The regnal-year sign (16-024) after _contract_ writes _of the year_, and the dating is read from it.

set.title: set truth in his mouth
set.note: No verb sign for _set_ or _place_. The plain hand (04-011) stands for the act.

truth.title: truth
truth.note: No sign means truth. 13-033, the balance with two pans, is the level account that Qe'aret's own sign (03-006) also draws. It reads as _order_ at least as readily as _truth_.

dominion.title: dominion
dominion.note: 03-029, a hand of power within a ring, carries no stated word. Read as power held, it stands for dominion.

against.title: came down upon
against.note: 01-066, two lines of men advancing against each other (q-z-t, _qezat_, battle), writes the war. At banner size its figures are small and thin; it is the least legible sign on the wall.

raged.title: raged
raged.note: No sign for rage. 01-015, the running man, writes the onrush.

chieftain.title: chieftains
chieftain.note: No sign for a chief. Written as _lord_ (01-013, the noble) with the foreigner (01-040) as determinative and the plural strokes.

took.title: took their herds
took.note: No sign for _take_. The plain hand (04-011) stands for seizing.

sandals.title: beneath his/your sandals
sandals.note: The sandal (15-009) is in the inventory but not drawn, so it prints nothing. Written with the walking legs (04-015) and, in register 3, the prostrate man (01-044). The sandal is the right sign once drawn.

mine.title: was the Gar-Au's
mine.note: The stela's refrain _and the canal was his_ is written with the enthroned Gar-Au (01-060) after the thing taken: _the margins, the Gar-Au_.

sea.title: the northern sea
sea.note: No sign for the sea. 10-022, water over broken rocks, reads as surf on a coast.

north.title: north
north.note: No sign for north. Spelled from the affix _-Miglet_: 10-009 (m-g), 13-001 (l), 13-005 (t). Its m-g value is from the sign's consonants; the spelling has no other source.

cedar.title: cedar
cedar.note: No sign for cedar. 13-037, the log (l-g-n, _lagun_), means timber of any kind.

rode.title: rode out
rode.note: No chariot or rider is drawn. The horse (05-005) stands for riding out.

beasts.title: the wild beasts
beasts.note: No lion and no wild bull is drawn: the bull survives only as a head (05-035), which already writes the herds. The beasts are the river-horse (05-018, _igelzut_), drawn half under the waterline; a river-horse in the fields is a beast that ravages crops. The river cat (05-040) is the only other wild beast drawn that belongs to no god; the jackal is Hezmu'iri's and the crocodile Chelsur's.

ravaged.title: that ravaged the herds and the fields
ravaged.note: No sign for ravaging. The line reads _the beasts of the herds and the fields_, and the vignette carries the hunt.

count.title: the beasts taken were counted
count.note: Written with the tally rod (13-035). No number is given in the approved text, so none is written. A count in strokes and tens (16-003) can follow the tally if the owner names one.

opened.title: opened the granaries
opened.note: No sign for opening. The plain hand (04-011) stands for the act.

seal.title: under his seal
seal.note: 13-032, the stamp seal (_qathur_), after the stela's _whose seal is on the granary_.

filled.title: filled its storehouses
filled.note: Written with 14-016, the heap of grain, before the granary. No sign means _fill_.

people.title: his people
people.note: No sign for a people. 01-068, the standing man with empty hands (z-l-r, _zelar_, the commoner), with the plural strokes, writes the common folk.

hunger.title: none of his people hungered
hunger.note: No sign for hunger or its absence. Written _his people: bread and life_, with the loaf (14-007) and the sprout of life (08-005).

gave.title: gave it altars
gave.note: No sign means _give_ to a god here; the offering table (14-009) with the plural strokes writes _altars_, and the giving is left unwritten.

lapis.title: lapis
lapis.note: No sign for lapis or any blue stone, and none is coined. The register reads _altars of gold_; the render can paint the altar sign lapis blue to carry the rest.

endowed.title: endowed it
endowed.note: Written with 13-032, the stamp seal (q-th-r, _qathur_, the seal and the warrant it closes): fields and herds given by sealed warrant.

head.title: at the head of the death-road
head.note: No sign for the head of a road. Written _at the road of the dead_: 10-020 (path between two stones) with 10-014 (the west, the realm of the dead) as determinative.

firstground.title: fire on the first ground
firstground.note: The hymn's _first ground_ is the primeval mound; 10-011 (mound on a flat) writes it.

son.title: my son
son.note: No sign means son. 01-067, a tall standing figure beside a small one (th-z), shows a parent with a child. The seated child (01-011) is the alternative.

every.title: every land, every foreign country
every.note: No sign for _every_. Written as plurals: lands, foreign countries.

level.title: the tablets level on the beam
level.note: 03-006 draws the Reading's _tablets level on the beam_ exactly, and it is also Qe'aret's sign. On a wall of the weighing both readings stand: the level account, and the goddess of the scale who holds it.

closed.title: closed
closed.note: 16-014, a closing bar under a row, writes the reader's _Closed_. No note states this use; the subject supports it.

open.title: open
open.note: 16-015, a gap in a bar, writes the reader's _Open_: the credit side left open. No note states this use; it is the broken bar beside the closing one.

owed.title: he went down owed
owed.note: No sign means _owed_. Written _went down, his account_ after _open_: the walking legs (04-015) and the bound heart (04-018). The reading rests on the open bar before it.
